name: 211. Encrypted Reasoning Fail-Soft Clears Paired Item IDs (failsoft-paired-ids)
description:
Bifrost's encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go) strips the replayed reasoning after a 400 and retries once on the same key.
It used to keep every other item's id. The upstream ties a stored turn's fc_/msg_ ids to that turn's reasoning item, so the retry still
failed with 400 "Item 'fc_..' of type 'function_call' was provided without its required 'reasoning' item" (seen from Warp on
openai/gpt-5.6-luna, and from Azure keys load-balanced across resources). The strip now clears those ids and keeps call_id.

The first case mints a stored turn (store left at its default) and captures its function_call. The replay cases send that call by its
id without its reasoning item, next to a synthetic reasoning payload the upstream cannot verify, which is what makes the strip fire.
Before the fix the retry carried the call id and got the 400 above; after it, the id is cleared and the turn completes.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT: the replay must omit the captured turn's own reasoning item. Replaying it lets the upstream pair the call, and the
case passes without the strip clearing anything. Leave tool_choice unset on turn 1: forcing the call makes the model skip
the reasoning item, so nothing pairs with the call.

The Anthropic cases pin the other side: Anthropic builds server_tool_use and mcp_tool_use ids from the item id, so a retry to any target
outside OpenAI's Responses API keeps item ids. Their web_search_call carries a Claude-shaped srvtoolu_ id, since Anthropic rejects any
other, and the synthetic reasoning item is what makes the strip fire. Before the gate the retry answered 400 "server_tool_use.id: Field required".

item.name: openai/gpt-5.4-mini /v1/responses turn 1 mints a stored tool call + capture - failsoft-paired-ids

exec: pm.test('turn 1 returns a reasoning item and the tool call it pairs with', function () {
pm.expect(types, 'no reasoning item for the call to pair with: ' + JSON.stringify(types)).to.include('reasoning');
var fc = output.filter(function (o) { return o.type === 'function_call' && o.id; })[0];
pm.collectionVariables.set('failsoftPairedIdsCall', JSON.stringify({ type: 'function_call', id: fc.id, call_id: fc.call_id, name: fc.name, arguments: fc.arguments }));

Look it up with the tool."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","name":"lookup_order","description":"Look up an order by id and return its status.","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"],"additionalProperties":false},"strict":true}],"reasoning":{"effort":"low"},"max_output_tokens":1024}
